title: A fixed Case B hydrogen screen at 10,000 K and up to three solar radii cannot keep a one-percent Thomson dip for one minute without ionization
abstract: We test the electron supply for a Thomson-scattering explanation of complex periodic variable dips. We derive a minimum recombination rate for arbitrary density profiles and covered area, and a maximum depth after ionization stops. For an illustrative 0.5-solar-radius star, a path of at most 3 solar radii, and Case B hydrogen at 10,000 K, a 1% depth needs at least 1.08e42 net ionizations per second. Ground-state photoionization must deposit at least 2.35e31 erg/s, or 0.259 times an illustrative stellar bolometric power. At 10% area coverage this rises to 2.85 times that power. With no ion source, no initial density can retain a 1% Thomson depth beyond 53.34 seconds. Retention for a 0.4-day rotation needs an effective recombination coefficient at least 648 times below Case B. We give an exact known-brightness extension and numerical checks. No observed cloud is fitted. Non-LTE recycling, continued ion supply, longer paths, other opacity and changing geometry can evade the tested assumptions. These are conditional bounds, not a general exclusion of gas.
